title: The 1787 text vests executive power in a president with a four-year term
summary: The 1787 text vests executive power in a president with a four-year term.
body: Article II, Section 1 of the 1787 transcription vests the executive power in a president, who holds office for a four-year term, together with a vice president chosen for the same term. The source says: "The executive Power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America." The electoral machinery that follows in the 1787 text was later amended. This card stops at the vesting and the term.
